title: Garment owners approve 'no work, no pay' closures from 15 November
excerpt: BGMEA says 147 factories with 300,000 workers could not run on Saturday. The wage board meets again on 16 November.
content:
Garment factory owners can close units and stop wages under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act from Sunday, 15 November, if unrest continues, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) decided at an emergency meeting in Dhaka on Saturday, The Daily Star reported.

Key facts

  • Meeting: nearly 1,500 factory owners attended at BGMEA's Uttara office. The knitwear association BKMEA backed the decision.
  • Factories hit on 14 November: 147 employing about 300,000 workers could not operate, BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan said. Of these, 55 had already invoked Section 13(1).
  • Ashulia on 15 November: 59 factories had suspended production, 18 of them under Section 13(1), according to the industrial police.
  • Gazipur: workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail Highway at Kaliakair for about two and a half hours on Saturday. Police used teargas and sound grenades and detained at least 20 people.

"Restoring normalcy is essential," Mr Khan said. Leaders of five labour federations urged workers on Friday to return to work so the wage board could do its job. They pointed to recent labour law changes that raised the annual increment from 5% to 9% and shortened the wage review cycle from five years to three.

Why it matters

Section 13(1) lets owners withhold pay while factories are shut, so hundreds of thousands of workers, most of them women, could lose income in the weeks before the new wage is set. Labour rights NGOs, legal aid groups and organisations running childcare, health and food support for garment workers may see more demand. The government's Tk 30 OMS rice sale for workers started on 13 November.

What to watch

The wage board's third meeting on 16 November, when owners are due to present their wage proposal against the workers' Tk 32,000, and how many factories close under Section 13(1) this week.
